Header.value: Human validation of LRH purpose coding
Classify what this passage does with the linear representation hypothesis (LRH). Several purposes may occur together. Base your decisions on the passage and its surrounding text.

Read the original PDF when extraction or context is unclear. Record the pages consulted in Notes. Choose Uncertain when you cannot decide. Submit saves a completed review and advances; partially entered choices are saved as drafts.
1. What kind of episode is this?

Substantive: a meaningful use or discussion of the LRH. Bibliography only: a reference entry or title. Structural fragment: navigation, a running header, or isolated text without an argumentative use. Insufficient context: the available text does not permit a decision.
Judge each purpose separately. Present and absent refer to the function of this passage, not to whether you accept the hypothesis.
Defines or formalizes the LRH, attributes it to prior work, frames a problem, or positions the paper within the literature.
Uses the LRH as a premise, justifies a method, or applies it to interpret a result.
Presents a theoretical explanation, an empirical test, or an evidential claim about the LRH. Evidence may come from earlier work and may oppose the hypothesis.
Limits or refines a formulation, extends or repairs it, or presents a challenge or counterevidence. Constructive extensions count here.
